dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees and retirees under the FEHBP, particularly those diagnosed with or at high risk for esophageal cancer.
dimensions.evidence: evaluation of... the total impact of esophageal cancer-related health care spending under the Federal Employee Health Benefits Program for Federal employees and retirees diagnosed with esophageal cancer

dimensions.assessment: Mandates a federal study and report rather than imposing direct nationwide regulatory or programmatic changes.
dimensions.evidence: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit a report to Congress that includes an evaluation of...

dimensions.assessment: Involves GAO resources to conduct the required study, but states no specific appropriation amounts.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit a report to Congress...

dimensions.assessment: Directs a federal agency (GAO) to evaluate specific health spending and screening data within an existing federal benefit program.
dimensions.evidence: evaluation of... how often individuals covered under the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program with medical records indicating such individuals are high-risk... undergo screening

dimensions.assessment: Fulfills a one-time reporting requirement due within one year of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit a report to Congress...

missing_information: Cost to the GAO to prepare and execute the required report.
importance_detail.rationale: This enacted law requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to produce a report for Congress evaluating esophageal cancer healthcare spending and screening rates under the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program.
